title: Distributed Safety Critical Control among Uncontrollable Agents Using Reconstructed Control Barrier Functions
evidence: Sec. III-C: a per-agent QP minimally modifies the nominal input so the reconstructed CBF holds, acting as a safety filter among controllable and uncontrollable agents (pedestrians, human-driven vehicles) to avoid inter-agent and obstacle collisions.
method: Distributed adaptive observer estimates other agents' states; coupled CBF is reconstructed on estimates with a prescribed-performance adaptive offset so reconstructed constraint implies the true one; CBF-QP safety filter per agent.
evaluation: Single simulation: 4 robots (1 uncontrollable), 3 obstacles; no baselines; qualitative trajectories, CBF values and inputs only; no hardware or solve time reported.
contribution: Fully distributed CBF-QP safety filter that reconstructs coupled barrier constraints from observer estimates, provably keeping a multi-agent system safe among uncontrollable agents.
flag: Borderline E2: evaluation is one illustrative simulation with no baselines or quantitative safety metrics; theory-first paper. No latency or compute figures. Simulation shows an input u4 for the 'uncontrollable' robot.

title: FORMULA: FORmation MPC with neUral barrier Learning for safety Assurance
evidence: Sec. III-B/IV-C: the learned NN-CBF is linearised at the current state and the MPC-CLF command is projected onto it via a minimum-deviation QP, so the safety filter overrides the nominal input to keep multi-robot formations collision-free.
method: Distributed MPC with CLF constraints for formation tracking, neural-network CBF (2x64 MLP) learned from sampled states as a decentralised safety filter, plus event-triggered deadlock resolver that perturbs the reference.
evaluation: Simulation only, 2D cluttered workspace, 3/5/9 unicycle robots; baselines APF, MPC-CBF, CLF+CBF-QP; safety rate, formation error, min distance (single rollouts); no timing or hardware reported.
contribution: Learning-enhanced distributed MPC that combines CLF formation tracking with a learned neural barrier safety filter, raising safety rate over APF, MPC-CBF and analytic CLF+CBF-QP baselines in simulation.
flag: Claims 'real-time feasibility with formal safety guarantees' but reports no compute times, control rates or hardware, and the NN-CBF is only trained on sampled states (no verification). Table I uses single rollouts. No real robots.

title: Game-Theoretic Safe Multiagent Motion Planning With Reachability Analysis for Dynamic and Uncertain Environments
evidence: Sec. III-C/V: a multi-agent forward reachable set (ellipsoidal error sets under bounded disturbance) is added as an exponential penalty so 'the MA-FRS penalties enforce non-overlapping safety regions'; deployed onboard Raspberry Pi 5 vehicles with per-step latency below the 0.2 s control period.
method: Decentralised motion planning as a dynamic potential game; neighbourhood-dominated iterated best response with epsilon-Nash convergence; reachability (MA-FRS) soft penalties for uncertainty-aware collision avoidance within receding-horizon MPC.
evaluation: Sim: 3-15 quadrotors, 50 MC runs, noise sweeps; baselines w/o-RE-DPG, PiLQR, Swarm-DRL; tracking cost, time efficiency, collision ratio. Real: 3-4 4WD vehicles on Raspberry Pi 5, <0.2 s/step, FRS 46-102 ms.
contribution: Reachability-enhanced dynamic potential game planner that adds multi-agent forward reachable sets as collision penalties, lowering collision ratios versus PiLQR and Swarm-DRL and running onboard Raspberry Pi 5 ground vehicles.
flag: Criterion (d) is borderline: onboard latency (<0.2 s, equal to control step) is reported but no explicit deadline analysis. Collision avoidance is a soft cost penalty, not a hard constraint or interception, despite abstract wording. Real experiments are 2D only (abstract says 2D and 3D). Extended version of the TII paper; check for duplicate record.

title: IDCAIS: Interdefender Collision-Aware Interception Strategy Against Multiple Attackers
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems
evidence: Sec. IV-A: when collisions cannot be avoided by the collision-aware assignment or attackers deviate from time-optimal play, an exponential-CBF QCQP adds a minimal correction delta-u to each defender's nominal control to keep defenders more than the collision radius apart.
method: MIQP defender-attacker assignment weighting time-optimal capture time against predicted inter-defender collision time (Algorithm 1 pre-filter); exponential CBF QCQP minimally corrects defender controls when collisions remain.
evaluation: MATLAB simulations, 2v2 and 3v3 damped double integrators; baseline CUDAA (collision-unaware); inter-defender distance, capture/escape outcomes; 68% collision avoidance over 20 configs; collision-time computation 61-1057 s for 15-30 attackers; no hardware.
contribution: Collision-aware defender assignment via MIQP plus an exponential-CBF minimal control correction that avoids inter-defender collisions during multi-attacker interception where collision-unaware assignment fails.
flag: Multi-agent hazard is inter-defender collision only; evaluation is scenario-based with one small statistic (68% over 20 configs). No forward-invariance proof (safety analysis deferred to future work); reported compute times are seconds to minutes, so not real-time. arXiv 2021, journal version 2026.

title: Manifold-constrained Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability Learning for Decentralized Multi-Agent Motion Planning
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. IV.C: the receding-horizon planner requires the learned HJ reachability value function, evaluated pairwise against each other agent, to stay above a safety buffer, and falls back to a conservative collision-evading control if the optimisation fails.
method: Manifold-constrained Hamilton-Jacobi reachability learned with a DeepReach-style solver; value function used as pairwise safety constraint in decentralized min-max receding-horizon trajectory optimisation (HaMMAR).
evaluation: Sim 2D ablation plus 2-5 UR5 manipulation tasks, 100 cases each; baselines Opt w/o HJR, AtlasRRT (dec./cent.); success, collision, planning time 0.10-0.17 s/step on Xeon w5-2455X + RTX 4070; 5 real-robot trials.
contribution: Learns manifold-constrained HJ reachability value functions and uses them as pairwise safety constraints in decentralized receding-horizon planning for multi-robot manipulation, with a conservative fail-safe fallback.
flag: Criterion (a) is via fail-safe fallback inside the planner, not a standalone filter; no explicit latency constraint (~100 ms/step on desktop GPU); offline HJR training time not reported.

title: Matrix Control Barrier Functions
evidence: Sec. VII-C/VIII-A: nominal tracking commands of five UAVs are passed through a CBF-SDP safety filter enforcing a matrix barrier (network connectivity LMI) plus pairwise collision CBFs, solved at every state update.
method: Matrix-valued control barrier functions for safe sets given by semidefinite/indefinite matrix inequalities; continuous CBF-SDP safety filter, also yielding continuous filters for Boolean (OR) barrier compositions.
evaluation: Five-quadrotor connectivity maintenance in sim and Crazyflie 2.1+ hardware (OptiTrack); qualitative vs scalar eigenvalue CBF (chattering); Clarabel SDP solve 1-2 ms on Ryzen 9 9950X at 240 Hz, offboard.
contribution: Extends control barrier functions to matrix inequalities, giving continuous SDP-based safety filters for nonsmooth and disjunctive safe sets, demonstrated on multi-UAV connectivity maintenance in hardware.
flag: Multi-agent filter is centralized and offboard; 1-2 ms solve time is reported but no explicit latency constraint is posed (criterion (d) not claimed); no quantitative baseline metrics.

title: Mean-Field Control Barrier Functions for Stochastic Multi-Agent Systems
evidence: Sec. II, Theorem 1 and Eq. 15: the nominal mean-field control field is corrected by a QP to lie in the admissible set guaranteeing forward invariance of the density-level safe set, keeping agents out of dangerous regions.
method: Mean-field control barrier functions for Fokker-Planck dynamics of stochastic multi-agent populations; QP correction of the control field with bounded-stability guarantee for density tracking.
evaluation: Numerical particle sims (720-820 agents) of coverage and shepherding, 50 runs each, baseline nominal controller only; metric fraction of agents in dangerous/goal regions; no hardware or runtime reported.
contribution: Derives mean-field control barrier functions for stochastic multi-agent densities governed by Fokker-Planck equations, with a QP safety correction and bounded stability under safety intervention.
flag: Density-level (mean-field) abstraction, simulation only, no timing or latency data; only baseline is the unfiltered nominal controller.

title: Multi-Robot Trajectory Planning via Constrained Bayesian Optimization and Local Cost Map Learning with STL-Based Conflict Resolution
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. IV, Alg. 2: for each robot pair an STL monitor is fed the pairwise state at each timestep and a conflict is recorded when robustness is negative, replacing the geometric collision test of K-CBS; conflicts are then resolved in the high-level search.
method: Two-stage multi-robot planner: cBOT single-robot sampling with GP-learned local cost/feasibility and constrained expected improvement; STL-KCBS conflict detection/resolution via STL robustness monitoring.
evaluation: Four sim environments, 2-50 robots, 10 trials, nine+ baselines (K-CBS/RRT/STGCS variants); success, runtime, path length; i7-10700 CPU; 3-robot indoor (42 ms) and 2-3 ASV lake trials.
contribution: Combines GP-guided constrained Bayesian sampling for single-robot kinodynamic planning with STL-monitored conflict detection and resolution for scalable, probabilistically complete multi-robot planning.
flag: Borderline E1: primarily an offline coordination planner; the safety element is STL-monitored inter-robot conflict detection, not runtime interception; no execution-time replanning loop; no human-in-the-loop.

title: R3R: Decentralized Multi-Agent Collision Avoidance with Infinite-Horizon Safety
evidence: Sec. III-C/Def. 10: a candidate trajectory is committed only if it passes a validity check (safe set, backup set reached, >=delta from neighbours' backup sets, R-bounded, avoids neighbours' committed trajectories); otherwise the agent keeps tracking its previous committed trajectory, giving infinite-horizon collision-free guarantees among asynchronously replanning agents (Thm. 1-2).
method: Decentralized asynchronous gatekeeper: nominal-plus-backup candidate trajectories validated against neighbours' committed trajectories; R-Boundedness ties planning radius to communication radius (R_comm = 3R_plan + delta) for infinite-horizon safety.
evaluation: Julia simulation, 8-128 Dubins vehicles, swap/city/willow-garage maps; baseline nonlinear MPC (Ipopt); metrics safety and success (100%/97-100%); avg 1.4 ms replan step, M2 MacBook Air; no hardware.
contribution: Decentralized gatekeeper with R-Boundedness certifies infinite-horizon collision avoidance for asynchronously replanning agents using only range-limited local communication, with per-step cost scaling in local density not team size.
flag: Safety mechanism is a commit-or-fallback shield (a) in a multi-agent collision setting (c); latency reported (1.4 ms avg) but no deadline/jitter model, no edge hardware, no handoff. Runtime of 32-agent case only; non-ideal networks deferred to future work.

title: Self-Navigation in Non-Adversarial Crowds: An Invariant Set-Based Approach
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology
evidence: Sec. III.A-B: at each planning instance the robot selects, from LiDAR returns of non-coordinating agents, the largest invariant disc that no static or constant-velocity moving point can enter within 1/f_p, then applies an input-constrained controller whose sublevel set is that disc (Thm. 1-2); Sec. IV.A reports ~57 ms per planning instance on a Raspberry Pi 4.
method: Input-constrained feedback controller for unicycle robots with disc-shaped invariant sublevel sets; per-cycle onboard LiDAR search for the feasible invariant disc nearest the target among non-coordinating moving agents.
evaluation: MATLAB multi-agent simulation (no collisions); 5 TurtleBot3/RPi4 with LiDAR, ViCON; baseline decoupled plan-and-react; metrics path length, curvature; ~57 ms/plan on RPi4; up to 3x parallel speedup on workstation.
contribution: Invariant-set-based reactive controller lets non-holonomic robots navigate crowds of non-coordinating agents from onboard LiDAR alone, with ~57 ms per planning cycle on a Raspberry Pi 4.
flag: Borderline (c)/E4: multi-agent only in that other agents are sensed obstacles with no coordination; multi-agent safety is empirical, formal result is single-robot invariance. Not a runtime monitor/deferral mechanism. Human appears only as an obstacle. arXiv title differs slightly from venue title (adds 'Non-Adversarial').

title: Stop Means Stop: Measuring and Repairing the Enforcement Gap in Agent-Framework Control Primitives
evidence: Sec. 5.1/5.3: SOUNDGATE requires every side effect to be submitted for admission at the tool boundary and executes it only on a release verdict; gated effects are held until an authenticated operator DECIDE, rejection is sticky, and cancelled/timed-out runs' effects are fenced; Sec. 4.2: 215/1,200 live runs leaked unmediated vs 0/1,200 through SOUNDGATE.
method: External Rust effect gate below the framework scheduler: hold-until-decided approval, sticky rejection, dedup-on-replay, fence-on-cancel; core verified with Verus, TLA+/TLC, TLAPS, Loom plus differential conformance.
evaluation: Six agent frameworks (LangGraph, LlamaIndex, MS Agent Framework, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, LangGraph.js); 1,000 random workflows, 1,200 live runs across 4 LLMs, injection tests, tau-bench; leak rate, false refusals (0); ~1 ms/gated write, 12k-26k admissions/s; hardware not retrieved.
contribution: Shows that human-approval gates, cancellation and timeouts in six LLM-agent frameworks fail to block parallel-branch side effects, and repairs this with SOUNDGATE, a verified effect gate adding ~1 ms per write with zero false refusals.
flag: Strong fit for (a) runtime interception, (c) safety evaluation of tool-calling agents, (e) human approval gates. Section 6 (performance hardware, p99 latency, tau-bench detail) could not be retrieved via WebFetch truncation; numbers taken from abstract/Sec. 4. Single author; v3 of a preprint, check for other queued versions.

title: TopoEvo: A Topology-Aware Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Framework for Root Cause Analysis in Microservices
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Web Services (ICWS)
evidence: Sec. III.D: a Hypothesis Planner, Metric/Log/Trace agents and a Judge agent run a Hypothesis-Evidence-Test workflow to separate initiating anomalies from amplified downstream symptoms; Sec. III.E: memory and test-time adaptation; no interception, halting or remediation of actions is described, only post-hoc diagnosis.
method: Topology-aware RCA: GAT localizer over service graph, VQ symptom tokens, multi-agent LLM Hypothesis-Evidence-Test workflow, self-evolving memory and test-time adaptation under topology drift.
evaluation: AIOps Challenge HipsterShop benchmark and a production incident dataset; baselines Nezha, Eadro, HolisticRCA, TAMO, RCAgent, mABC; ACC@1/3/5 (75.66% vs 72.22%); GPT-4o, A100 80GB; latency metric defined but not reported.
contribution: TopoEvo diagnoses microservice root causes under cascading failures and topology drift by combining graph-based localization, symptom tokens and a multi-agent hypothesis-testing LLM workflow with self-evolving memory.
flag: Multi-agent LLM pipeline for offline root cause analysis; cascading failures are diagnosed after the fact, no runtime safety interception, deferral, latency constraint or handoff. Multi-agent only as an analysis workflow (protocol v1.2). Nearest overlap is graph representation of service dependency state (b, weak).
